subject.mainFocus: Durable Project definition for the discrete-work lifecycle independent of any one System implementation, application, datastore, deployment, or repository location.
subject.description: Defines Task Assignment and Tracking as the durable Klinswork Project responsible for reliable operational knowledge and control of discrete work, including purpose, operational function, scope, boundaries, Work Queue context, Resource references, shared dependencies, current state, evidence discipline, history, authority routing, unresolved questions, and next work.

documentSummary.purpose: Provide the authoritative human-readable Project definition and current interpretation for Task Assignment and Tracking while keeping intrinsic identity, Resource routing, cross-entity relationships, current Work Queue implementation truth, roadmap direction, and execution evidence with their own authorities.
documentSummary.scope: Project purpose, discrete-work operational function, scope, functional boundaries, Work Queue System context, Resource references and authority rules, shared Building Map/employee dependencies, current Project-definition state, evidence classes, historical framing, Work Unit/roadmap/plan separation, resume-work guidance, unresolved questions, and next work.
documentSummary.summary: Task Assignment and Tracking is a Klinswork Project concerned with reliable operational knowledge and control of discrete work from intake through responsibility, performance, completion, verification, history, reporting, and downstream effects. Its principal known System is Work Queue. The Project remains distinct from Work Queue, Scheduling, Inventory Management, employee/personnel authority, Building Map / Locations, Documentation infrastructure, and Meadows Housekeeping. The Project-level definition now consists of Project Identity, local README, human-readable Project Summary, the governing implementation-plan pair, and this structured companion; Work Queue current-state System documentation and full discovery/Viewer validation remain.
documentSummary.confidence: high for documented Project-definition facts; detailed current Work Queue implementation state remains intentionally bounded and requires System-level/current-evidence verification

keyPoints.title: Task Assignment and Tracking is the Project
keyPoints.description: Task Assignment and Tracking is the durable Project; Work Queue is its principal known System, not a synonym for the Project.

keyPoints.title: Project ID remains unassigned
keyPoints.description: The permanent PROJ-### value is intentionally blank until formal allocation; names, folders, relationships, Work Queue, Resources, and prior provisional numbering must not be used to invent one.

keyPoints.title: Operational function is the discrete-work lifecycle
keyPoints.description: The Project covers identifying work, establishing context and responsibility, tracking performance and state, preserving notes/evidence, completing and verifying work, retaining history, and using that information operationally.

keyPoints.title: Project boundaries are functional
keyPoints.description: Scheduling, Inventory Management, employee/personnel authority, Building Map / Locations, Documentation, Meadows Housekeeping, and Work Queue remain distinct even when they are tightly related to the Project.

keyPoints.title: Current System truth and roadmap intent are separate
keyPoints.description: The Work Queue System Summary should answer what Work Queue is now; the Work Queue roadmap answers what it should become. Planned roadmap capabilities must not be presented as implemented merely because they are documented.

keyPoints.title: Building Map is a shared dependency, not owned scope
keyPoints.description: Task Assignment and Tracking depends on a complete, stable shared location model for mature location-aware behavior but does not become the owner of Building Map / Locations.

keyPoints.title: Resource identity is separate from Project identity
keyPoints.description: Applications, spreadsheets, datasets, source code, deployments, technical manuals, and other implementation artifacts are Resources whose stable identity and routing belong in the Resource Registry.

keyPoints.title: Evidence classes remain explicit
keyPoints.description: Historical implementation evidence, planning/design evidence, and current implementation evidence answer different questions and must not be silently merged.

keyPoints.title: Roadmaps, Work Units, and implementation plans have different granularity
keyPoints.description: System Roadmaps provide durable future direction, Roadmap Areas organize capability domains, Work Units track bounded capability outcomes, and implementation plans define intended execution method.

keyPoints.title: Next layer is Work Queue current-state documentation
keyPoints.description: After this Project Summary companion is installed and validated, the next Project Definition work is the Work Queue README, current-state System Summary, and System Summary sidecar.

general.summary: This record describes the Task Assignment and Tracking Project independently of any single app. It explains why the Project exists, where Work Queue fits, what neighboring functions remain separate, what is known now, what is planned, and what remains unresolved.

sections.title: 1. Document purpose and authority
sections.contentSummary: Defines the Project Summary as the human-readable explanatory authority for Project purpose, scope, boundaries, current interpretation, historical framing, and unresolved Project-definition questions while preserving distributed authority.

sections.title: 2. Project identity context
sections.contentSummary: Defines Task Assignment and Tracking as a Project, preserves its blank/unassigned permanent Project ID, and separates identity from hierarchy, System, Resources, environment, deployment, lifecycle, and implementation.

sections.title: 3. Purpose
sections.contentSummary: States the purpose as reliable operational knowledge and control of discrete work across the full lifecycle.

sections.title: 4. Operational function
sections.contentSummary: Models the controlled transition from identified work through context, review, responsibility, performance, completion, preserved history, and operational use.

sections.title: 5. Scope
sections.contentSummary: Defines in-scope lifecycle, evidence, history, search/reporting, recurring work, integrations, administration/integrity, and documentation concerns and distinguishes adjacent functions.

sections.title: 6. Project boundaries
sections.contentSummary: Separates Task Assignment and Tracking from Scheduling, Inventory Management, employee/personnel authority, Building Map / Locations, Documentation, Meadows Housekeeping, and Work Queue.

sections.title: 7. Paperwork and human-process parallel
sections.contentSummary: Preserves the real operational process as broader than digital participation and recognizes paper, verbal, observational, photographic, and system-originated inputs.

sections.title: 8. Principal System: Work Queue
sections.contentSummary: Places Work Queue as the principal known System and records a bounded set of supported high-level current System facts while deferring detailed current-state verification to the System Summary.

sections.title: 9. Resources
sections.contentSummary: Identifies current Work Queue Resource references and preserves Resource Registry authority for identity, current location, routing, deployment, and version facts.

sections.title: 10. Current state
sections.contentSummary: Separates operational/current implementation state, planned System direction, and Project-definition/documentation state.

sections.title: 11. Current records and authority routing
sections.contentSummary: Routes identity, orientation, Project narrative, structured sidecar interpretation, System records, implementation plans, and execution history to distinct authorities.

sections.title: 12. Relationships and integration context
sections.contentSummary: Describes Operations, Work Queue, Scheduling, Inventory Management, Employee Profile, Building Map / Locations, QR reporting, bounded OpenAI assistance, and Documentation as contextual relationships.

sections.title: 13. Building Map dependency
sections.contentSummary: Explains why shared stable location identity is important to task operations and why dependence on Building Map does not transfer ownership into this Project.

sections.title: 14. Roadmap, Work Units, and implementation plans
sections.contentSummary: Separates durable System direction, roadmap areas, bounded Work Units, implementation plans, and formal Work Implementation Sessions.

sections.title: 15. History and architectural evolution
sections.contentSummary: Preserves historical Tasker/application-centered terminology while expressing the current Project/System/Resource interpretation and evidence-class rules.

sections.title: 16. Current operational evidence boundary
sections.contentSummary: Limits the Project Summary's implementation claims and defers exact Work Queue architecture, deployment, datastore, behavior, permissions, tests, and unresolved issues to current System evidence.

sections.title: 17. How to enter or resume work on this Project
sections.contentSummary: Defines progressive context-loading routes for Project, roadmap, current implementation, and Building Map-related work.

sections.title: 18. Project Definition exemplar role
sections.contentSummary: Defines Task Assignment and Tracking → Work Queue as the second Project Definition exemplar after Inventory Management → Inventory 3.0.

sections.title: 19. Unresolved questions
sections.contentSummary: Keeps Project/System identity, relationships, Resource reconciliation, lifecycle, permissions, integrations, evidence, Viewer/Profile, template, and implementation-history questions explicitly open.

sections.title: 20. Next work
sections.contentSummary: Directs work from the Project Summary sidecar into Work Queue current-state documentation, discovery/Viewer validation, Registry/architecture reconciliation, session closure, and later product-planning follow-on.

sections.title: 21. Resulting Project state
sections.contentSummary: Shows the layered Project Definition structure and explains how it preserves Project intelligibility through changes in Work Queue, deployment, datastore, repository, relationships, environment, and integrations.

sections.title: 22. Current canonical interpretation
sections.contentSummary: Summarizes the current semantic hierarchy from Klinswork through Operations and Task Assignment and Tracking to Work Queue and its Resources.
